newsitem.title: UK: Britain helps with possible Zaire evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Britain helps with possible Zaire evacuation.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday it had decided to send boats and hovercraft to prepare for a possible evacuation of foreign nationals from Zaire.
An advance team of British military personnel was already in Kinshasa, the Congo capital Brazzaville and in Gabon, a defence ministry spokesman said.
"We have decided to deploy a small number of boats and hovercraft and associated personnel to Brazzaville over the weekend," the spokesman said.
There were no immediate plans to evacuate the 260 Britons and 200 other nationals for which Britain has consular responsibility in Zaire.
But Britain, whose plans had the backing of allied nations, wanted the force to be in place should such an operation become necessary, the spokesman said.
He declined to give details of how many boats, hovercraft and personnel would be sent because plans were still being finalised.
But the ministry confirmed there were already 11 British military personnel in Kinshasa, 16 in Brazzaville and one or two in the Gabonese capital, Libreville.
Rebels in Zaire have agreed to talks with the shaky regime of President Mobutu Sese Seko but have refused to accept a prior ceasefire.
After five months of revolt, fighters loyal to rebel leader Laurent Kabila control about a quarter of Zaire.
